facts.t: The Ninth Schedule grew from 13 to nearly 285
facts.d: It began in 1951 with thirteen state land-reform laws. It now holds close to 285 entries, including laws on sugarcane pricing, urban land ceilings and Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation. The device built for agrarian reform became a general-purpose shelter.

facts.t: The mini-Constitution changed 54 provisions at once
facts.d: The 42nd Amendment of 1976, passed during the Emergency, is the single largest constitutional change India has seen — it rewrote the Preamble, curbed the courts, and tried to place amendments beyond judicial reach altogether.

facts.t: Property is the only Fundamental Right ever deleted
facts.d: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 and relocated property to Article 300A. It is now a constitutional and legal right available to all persons, not a Fundamental Right — and, notably, it protects non-citizens too.

bank.q: Which case marked the first application of the Basic Structure Doctrine to strike down a constitutional amendment?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
bank.e: Kesavananda formulated the doctrine but upheld the 24th Amendment. Its first actual application came two years later, when the 39th Amendment shielding the election of high offices from judicial review was struck down.

bank.q: Arrange the following judgments in correct chronological order:
items: Golak Nath v. State of Punjab
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
bank.e: Golak Nath (1967) → Kesavananda (1973) → Minerva Mills (1980) → Waman Rao (1981).

bank.q: Match List I (amendment) with List II (what it did):
pairs: 1. Abolished privy purses by inserting Article 363A
2. Made Article 13 inapplicable to constitutional amendments
3. Made the election of high offices non-justiciable
4. Inserted Article 31C giving primacy to Articles 39(b) and (c)
bank.e: 24th → Articles 13(4) and 368(3), negativing Golak Nath; 25th → Article 31C; 26th → abolition of privy purses via Article 363A; 39th → immunising the elections of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker.

bank.q: With reference to the 42nd Amendment, 1976, consider the following statements:
s: It added the words socialist, secular and integrity to the Preamble.
It gave all Directive Principles primacy over Articles 14, 19 and 31.
It inserted Articles 368(4) and (5) declaring amendments unchallengeable and constituent power unlimited.
bank.e: All three are correct. Clauses (4) and (5) were the direct attempt to nullify Kesavananda, and both were struck down in Minerva Mills.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the 44th Amendment, 1978?
o: It removed property as a Fundamental Right
It restored property to Part III as a qualified right
bank.e: Property was not restored to Part III. It became a constitutional and legal right for all persons under Article 300A — outside the Fundamental Rights chapter and outside Article 32.

bank.as: Minerva Mills restored Article 31C to its pre-42nd Amendment position.
bank.rs: The Court held that Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles must be read harmoniously.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Extending 31C to all DPSPs would have subordinated Part III wholesale, destroying the balance the Court identified as itself part of the basic structure.

bank.q: The cut-off date fixed in Waman Rao (1981) for challenging Ninth Schedule laws is:
bank.e: 24 April 1973 — the date Kesavananda was decided. Laws inserted before that date are protected; those added after are open to basic-structure challenge.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about Golak Nath (1967):
s: It held that constitutional amendments are law within the meaning of Article 13(2).
It overruled Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh.
It applied the doctrine of prospective overruling.
bank.e: All three are correct. Golak Nath gave Fundamental Rights a transcendental position and barred future amendments to Part III — while leaving past amendments untouched through prospective overruling.

bank.q: The 99th Amendment establishing the NJAC was struck down in:
o: I. R. Coelho v. State of TN (2007)
bank.e: The Fourth Judges Case — SC AoR Association (2015) — held independence of the judiciary to be part of the basic structure and struck down the NJAC.

bank.q: Which one of the following was NOT held in Property Owners Association v. State of Maharashtra (2024)?
o: Article 31C's position as settled by Kesavananda and Minerva Mills remains valid
Not all private property is a material resource of the community under Article 39(b)
Article 31 is revived as a Fundamental Right
The scope for government acquisition is thereby limited
bank.e: Article 31 was not revived — it remains deleted by the 44th Amendment. The Court limited the reach of Article 39(b) without restoring property to Part III.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the First Amendment, 1951:
s: It inserted Article 15(4), nullifying the effect of Champakam Dorairajan.
It added grounds of restriction to Article 19(2), responding to Romesh Thappar.
It inserted Article 31B and with it the Ninth Schedule.
bank.e: All three are correct. The First Amendment was a coordinated legislative response to a series of early judgments that had struck at reservations, at press restrictions and at land reform.

bank.q: I. R. Coelho (2007) added which element to the Waman Rao position?
o: It advanced the cut-off date to 1976
Post-1973 Ninth Schedule laws can also be tested against Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21 specifically
It restored blanket immunity to all Ninth Schedule laws
It held that ordinary laws cannot violate the basic structure
bank.e: Coelho confirmed Waman Rao's date and went further — post-1973 entries face a concrete rights-impact analysis under Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21, not merely an abstract basic-structure inquiry. The last option is Madras Bar Association (2015).

bank.as: Sajjan Singh (1965) reaffirmed that a constitutional amendment is not law under Article 13(2).
bank.rs: The petitioners had argued that the 17th Amendment curtailed High Court powers and therefore required state ratification.
bank.e: Both are true, but the Reason states the contention raised rather than the ground of the holding. The Court reaffirmed Shankari Prasad on the Article 13 question; the ratification argument was a separate limb.
